T-0961. Moses and Kirkland, History of Chicago, Illinois, vol. 1 (Chicago: Munsell, 1895), printed pages 78-79: the table headed LIST OF ACTUAL SETTLERS AT CHICAGO, PRIOR TO 1830, transcribed row by row. T-0581 found this table and recorded its EXISTENCE and the rule it was built on as claim bk_mose1_014, and deliberately did not transcribe it: a roster with a nativity and an arrival year per person is records-shaped, and reading it is its own demonstration. This is that demonstration.

WHY IT IS `records` AND NOT `claims`. The books domain holds prose and this volume is prose everywhere else in it. These two pages are not: they are a printed table with four columns, and the unit is a ROW read as it stands, which is the shape research_domains.py fixes for a list. Every other reading in this domain sits under claims/ for the same reason in reverse.

WHAT THE REMARKS COLUMN DOES AND DOES NOT LICENSE — the distinction this file turns on. The cells say `Paid taxes in 1825`, `voted in 1826`, `voted in 1830`. Those are CIVIC ACTS at dates, and every one of them falls between five and ten years before the scene. Paying a Peoria County tax in 1825 says a man was assessed in 1825; voting in 1830 says he was on that poll. NEITHER IS A RESIDENCE ON 1835-07-01, singly or together, and nothing in this file is graded as though it were. The table's own preamble is the cleanest statement of its limit: it names those `known to have had a residence at the settlement` BEFORE 1830, and it excludes Gurdon S. Hubbard by name because he `did not take up a permanent residence until 1832` — the compiler drawing the same line this project draws, sixty years earlier and in the other direction.

THE TABLE IS AN 1895 COMPILATION AND CREDITS ITS SOURCE THREE LINES ABOVE ITSELF: Hurlbut's Chicago Antiquities, pp. 37-8. Every row is transcription_mediated and none is scan_verified; the tier-3 grade of the source record is the ceiling here as everywhere else in this file's domain.

THE DITTO MARKS ARE RESOLVED AND SAID TO BE RESOLVED. Nine cells in this table are the printer's ditto, and each is recorded as what it repeats with `(ditto)` on the value and the row above named in the note. Two of those resolutions are worth distrusting and the notes say so. THE OCR IS REPAIRED IN `normalized` AND NOWHERE ELSE: `verbatim` is the scan's own line, byte for byte, and the gate rebuilds it out of the committed text at the locator.
generated_by: hand — T-0961. The `verbatim` of every record was filled programmatically from the committed text at its own locator, as T-0581 filled this volume's quotes, so that no transcription step stands between the file and the gate. Everything else in each record is authored: the cell readings, the ditto resolutions, the OCR repairs and the notes.
